The document omits "Campogalliano". Is omission of a place-name component "different entity"? No — it's the same company, just a shorter form. Spelling drift, accent differences = same-entity. That's about numbers. For same-entity name drift, which value? The document is the legal instrument (per different-entity rule, best_value = document's). But for same-entity, presumably we'd prefer the register's canonical form? Actually the rules don't explicitly say for same-entity name drift. Hmm.

For same-entity, options: register canonical form is typically preferred for the fused record since register is canonical database row. But the certificate is the legal instrument... The rules only specify best_value for document-noise (register) and different-entity (document) and number format same-entity (register). For accent drift same-entity, the register value "Societa Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l" seems the canonical fuller form. Since same-entity, best_value = register's canonical form seems reasonable — the register is the canonical database row, and the fuller name is more identifying. Also register value lacks the accent (likely normalization), while the document is the legal doc with proper accent "Società". Hmm, which to pick?

I think the register's value as canonical form is the best choice: it's fuller (includes Campogalliano, the distinctive place element) and the register is canonical. I'll go: verdict same-entity, best_value = register value "Societa Cooperativa Bilanciai Campogalliano a.r.l", why: same Italian cooperative with accent/omission drift; register form is canonical and more complete.
